intended_object: The integral Spin group attached to the ℤ_p-lattice L spanned by a basis b of a quadratic space (V, Q) over ℚ_p. It is the set of s ∈ Spin(Q) whose image in O(Q) preserves L, i.e. the preimage of the lattice stabilizer O(L) under Spin(Q) → O(Q). Source: the docstring and module documentation (O'Meara §101).
explanation:
The body is `(integralOrthogonalSubgroup Q b).comap (spinToOrthogonal Q)`, which is exactly the "full preimage" the docstring describes.

- **The orthogonal subgroup.** `integralOrthogonalSubgroup Q b` contains the isometries g for which the matrices of both g and g⁻¹ in the basis b have entries in ℤ_p (`mem_integralOrthogonalSubgroup_iff`). This is the same as g preserving the ℤ_p-span L of b, so it is the standard O(L).
- **The projection.** `spinToOrthogonal` is the vector representation by Clifford conjugation, Spin(Q) → O(Q). It is well defined over ℚ_p for every p, including p = 2, because 2 is invertible in ℚ_p.

So membership means exactly that the orthogonal action of s, and of its inverse, preserves the lattice. The module doc says explicitly that this is the intended notion, not a condition on the coordinates of the Clifford element itself.

**Degenerate case.** When V = 0, Spin is trivial and the subgroup is all of it, as expected.

**Generality.** The setting is ℚ_p, inherited from the library's `integralOrthogonalSubgroup`. The same construction would work over any non-archimedean local field or any lattice. However, the definition is only a pullback of the library's existing integral orthogonal family. The ℚ_p setting is what its use requires: varying the prime p for rational quadratic forms, and compact-open families at almost every prime. Mathlib has no integral orthogonal or integral Spin subgroup in greater generality to point to. So I don't count this as too narrow, and the definition is a faithful formalization.
